# Fixing a running toilet

## What was wrong

Upstairs loo kept trickling into the pan after every flush and the cistern refilled itself every 20 min or so with a hiss. Water meter test: everything off, read the meter at 21:00 and 07:00. Used 0.27 m³ overnight, which is about 32 litres an hour wasted. That's money straight down the drain on a meter.

## Diagnosis

Two possible culprits, did the food colouring test to tell which:
- Couple of drops of blue food colouring in the cistern, no flush, wait 15 min
- Blue in the pan = flush valve seal is letting by
- No blue but water going down the overflow = fill valve not shutting off

Got blue in the pan. So it was the flush valve seal, not the fill valve. Same day as the [[Leaky tap washer]] job so I had the water off anyway.

## Parts

- Cistern is Ideal Standard, flush valve is a Siamp 34 (stamped on the side)
- Siamp replacement seal, 63mm, Screwfix item 49271, £4.99
- Ended up also replacing the fill valve while I was in there because the float arm was gummed up: Fluidmaster 400UK bottom entry, £11.98
- Isolation valve on the cistern feed was seized solid, so main stop tap off under the stairs

## The job

1. Turned off, flushed, sponged the rest out
2. Flush valve on a Siamp twists a quarter turn anticlockwise and lifts out. No need to take the cistern off the pan, which was a relief
3. Old seal was warped and had a groove worn in it. New seal pushes on the bottom
4. Fill valve: undid the tap connector underneath, back nut off, swapped, set the float so the water stops 25mm below the overflow
5. Replaced the seized isolation valve too, 15mm compression, £2.40

## After

Meter overnight test again: 0.003 m³. Basically nothing. Flush is quieter as well. Total parts £19.37.

Note: if it starts running again, check the chain/cable length on the button before buying anything. Water bill line in [[Budget spreadsheet]] should drop from April.
